statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-4873: when a transfer that requires TLS (CURLOPT_USE_SSL) follows a clear-text IMAP, POP3 or SMTP transfer to the same host, libcurl can reuse the existing unencrypted connection and send the data without TLS (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-4873.html). It affects curl 7.20.0 to 8.19.0 and was fixed in curl 8.20.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/507e7be573b0a76fca597b75ff7cb27a66e7d865, which adds a TLS requirement (req_tls) to the connection-reuse match in lib/url.c. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI Alpine 3.23 main repository publishes curl builds 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. IMAP, POP3 and SMTP are built in every one of them (the objects built from imap.c, pop3.c and smtp.c in the static libcurl.a shipped in curl-static define functions). In the debug information shipped in curl-dbg, on x86_64 and aarch64, the connection-match structure has no TLS-requirement member in 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0 and 8.19.0-r0, has the req_tls member the fix adds in 8.20.0-r0 and 8.20.0-r1, and has it under the name require_tls, which upstream gave it later, from 8.21.0-r0 on. So 8.20.0-r0, the first build of curl 8.20.0, is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-4873: when a transfer that requires TLS (CURLOPT_USE_SSL) follows a clear-text IMAP, POP3 or SMTP transfer to the same host, libcurl can reuse the existing unencrypted connection and send the data without TLS (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-4873.html). It affects curl 7.20.0 to 8.19.0 and was fixed in curl 8.20.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/507e7be573b0a76fca597b75ff7cb27a66e7d865, which adds a TLS requirement (req_tls) to the connection-reuse match in lib/url.c. Debian backported the fix to trixie in 8.14.1-2+deb13u4 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4873). The DHI curl packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie curl 8.14.1-2; as of 2026-11-27 the DHI Debian repository publishes three of them (the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and two rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7) for amd64 and arm64, all later than 8.14.1-2+deb13u4, and each ships a Debian changelog that records the fix under 8.14.1-2+deb13u4. In the debug information of libcurl4t64 and libcurl3t64-gnutls of all three builds, on amd64 and arm64, the connection-match structure has a TLS-requirement member (req_tls in the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5, may_tls and require_tls in the rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7), which Debian's own unfixed 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 libcurl4t64 build (amd64) does not have. Every published build carries the fix, so the fixed version is the lowest published one, the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5.
